plants.credit_line: Devil's claw (Harpagophytum procumbens), recently dehisced capsule (trample-burr), Manie van der Schijff Botanical Garden, University of Pretoria. Photo: SAplants, Wikimedia Commons, [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0).
plants.why: Clear SAplants species photograph of the diagnostic dehisced capsule (trample-burr), the hooked fruit that gives devil's claw its name. Print-ready resolution; preferred over the 1846 Icones selectae plantarum plate on Commons (File:Harpagophytum procumbens00.jpg), which is only 831×1080 px.

plants.commons_title: File:Pelargonium sidoides - Lyman Plant House, Smith College - DSC01935.jpg
plants.credit_line: African geranium (Pelargonium sidoides), botanical specimen, Lyman Plant House, Smith College, Northampton, Massachusetts. Photo: Daderot, Wikimedia Commons, [CC0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/).
plants.why: High-resolution greenhouse specimen photograph under an explicit CC0 dedication, labelled Pelargonium sidoides at the Lyman Plant House. Preferred for licence clarity (CC0) at print-ready size, showing the characteristic dark flowers and grey-green leaves of umckaloabo.

plants.credit_line: African potato (Hypoxis hemerocallidea), plant in flower, grassland, Brummeria, Pretoria, Gauteng. Photo: SAplants, Wikimedia Commons, [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0).
plants.why: Clear SAplants field photograph of a flowering plant in Pretoria grassland, under the accepted name Hypoxis hemerocallidea. Shows the diagnostic yellow star-flowers and strap leaves of African potato at print-ready resolution.

plants.credit_line: African ginger (Siphonochilus aethiopicus; syn. Kaempferia aethiopica), flower, SW Burkina Faso. Photo: Marco Schmidt, Wikimedia Commons, [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0).
plants.why: Marco Schmidt field photograph of the flower, filed under the synonym Kaempferia aethiopica but described on Commons as Siphonochilus aethiopicus. Highest-resolution freely licensed flower image available for this scarce species on Commons.

plants.commons_title: File:Warburgia salutaris, loof en blomme, Manie van der Schijff BT, b.jpg
plants.credit_line: Pepper-bark tree (Warburgia salutaris), foliage and flowers, Manie van der Schijff Botanical Garden, University of Pretoria. Photo: JMK, Wikimedia Commons, [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0).
plants.why: JMK photograph of foliage and flowers together at Manie van der Schijff Botanical Garden, under an explicit Warburgia salutaris filename. Better ID plate than bark-only shots of the same tree.

plants.credit_line: African cherry (Prunus africana), flowers, Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden, Cape Town. Photo: SAplants, Wikimedia Commons, [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0).
plants.why: Clear SAplants photograph of flowers at Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden, under the accepted name Prunus africana. Print-ready resolution showing axillary flower clusters for species confirmation of African cherry / red stinkwood.
